table.name: atom
table.purpose: One row per atom in a set of molecular structures: each row pairs a molecule identifier (col_002) with an atom index (embedded in col_001) and a chemical element symbol (col_003). Likely the atom table of a molecular/chemistry database, referenced by t03 (e.g. bonds or measurements).

col_001.name: atom_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Composite code 'TRxxx_n' = molecule identifier TRxxx plus an atom index n within that molecule; unique per row (e.g. TR031_31 = molecule TR031, atom 31). Referenced by t03.col_001 and t03.col_002.

col_002.name: molecule_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the molecule this atom belongs to (TRxxx, 444 distinct molecules); matches the prefix of col_001. References t04.col_001, presumably a molecules table.

col_003.name: element_symbol
col_003.description: Chemical element symbol of the atom (h, c, o, n, cl, br, si, p, zn, ...). 21 distinct elements; hydrogen and carbon dominate, consistent with organic molecules.

table.purpose: Rows keyed by a composite code (e.g. TR031_18_36) that pairs a parent entity TRxxx (matching t04) with two numbers, likely a segment/interval between two positions or stops. Referenced by t03. The exact domain (e.g. transport routes, transcripts) is unresolved from the data alone.

col_001.name: segment_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Composite code: parent entity code (TRxxx) plus two numbers (e.g. TR031_18_36), suggesting a segment/interval between two positions on the entity referenced by col_002. Referenced by t03.col_003.

col_002.name: parent_id
col_002.description: Code of the parent entity (TRxxx), matching t04.col_001. Many rows per parent (up to 175).

table.name: trace_step_transitions
table.purpose: Each row records a transition (directly-follows edge) between two steps within a trace: col_001 is the source step, col_002 the successor step, and col_003 the identifier of the step-pair/edge, which is also catalogued in t02. The TRxxx prefix groups rows by trace (matching t01, likely the trace or step table). This is consistent with a process/event-log style schema where t01 lists individual steps, t02 lists distinct step pairs, and t03 lists every observed occurrence of a pair in sequence. The exact domain (process mining, workflow, etc.) is inferred from the TR###_n pattern, not stated explicitly.

col_001.name: from_step_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the first (source) step of a consecutive step pair within a trace. Format TR<trace>_<step>, referencing t01.col_001 (many-to-one). Duplicated with col_002 in some rows only when a step follows itself.

col_002.name: to_step_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the second (target/successor) step of the pair, same format TR<trace>_<step>, referencing t01.col_001. In every sampled row it is the numerically next or later step number of the same trace as col_001.

col_003.name: step_pair_id
col_003.description: Identifier of the step pair/edge, formed by concatenating the two step ids: TR<trace>_<step1>_<step2>. References t02.col_001 (many-to-one), so t02 appears to be a catalog of distinct step pairs. Near-unique here (uniqueness 0.5) because most pairs occur once per trace.

table.name: molecule
table.purpose: Unresolved. The table has only two columns: a unique transaction/record identifier (TRnnn) and a binary sign flag. It is referenced by t01 and t02, suggesting it is a lookup or header table for transactions, but the evidence is insufficient to determine its business meaning.

col_001.name: transaction_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Unique text identifier with pattern TRnnn (e.g. TR000, TR477), one per row. Referenced by t01.col_002 and t02.col_002, so it identifies a transaction/record that other tables link to. The 'TR' prefix suggests a transaction or trial number, but the exact entity is unresolved.
